node_audit.judge_reason: The genuinely new element is the tau-admission rule, which uses the near-degeneracy of McLachlan distances to pick topology-local operators inside the adaptive dynamics loop. Its measured effect is modest and inconsistent (Topology B mean 1.77 to 1.63, and negative on MFIM hz0/B). The larger gains come from persistent permutation tracking and lookahead-like locality scoring, both standard in routers such as SABRE and t|ket>. The contribution adds real scientific content (systematic two-topology quantification, ablations, failure modes) but with limited novelty relative to the compilation and hardware-aware ADAPT literature, and there is no comparison against a lookahead router.
